activities.title: Acids and bases in the laboratory
activities.summary: Test HCl, H₂SO₄, HNO₃, CH₃COOH, NaOH, Ca(OH)₂, KOH, Mg(OH)₂, NH₄OH with indicators; record colours in Table 2.1.

activities.title: Olfactory indicators
activities.summary: Prepare onion cloth strips; test with dilute HCl and NaOH; try vanilla essence and clove oil.

activities.title: Zinc with dilute sulphuric acid
activities.summary: React zinc with dilute H₂SO₄; collect and test hydrogen gas by burning.

activities.title: Zinc with sodium hydroxide
activities.summary: Warm zinc granules with NaOH solution; collect and test hydrogen gas evolved.

activities.title: Metal carbonates with acid
activities.summary: React Na₂CO₃ and NaHCO₃ with dilute HCl; pass CO₂ through lime water.

activities.title: Acid–base neutralisation
activities.summary: Add HCl to phenolphthalein–NaOH; observe colour change; add NaOH again.

activities.title: Copper oxide with acid
activities.summary: Add dilute HCl to copper oxide; observe blue-green solution of copper(II) chloride.

activities.title: Non-metallic oxide with base
activities.summary: Observe CO₂ from Activity 2.5 reacting with calcium hydroxide (lime water).

activities.title: Acid/base conductivity
activities.summary: Test conductivity of dilute HCl, glucose, alcohol, and dilute NaOH with a bulb circuit.

activities.title: Dilution of acid and base
activities.summary: Add concentrated H₂SO₄ to water and NaOH pellets to water; note temperature change.

activities.title: pH paper on solutions
activities.summary: Test dilute HCl, NaOH, lemon juice, vinegar, soap solution, and milk with pH paper.

activities.title: Soil pH testing
activities.summary: Collect soil samples; shake with water; filter; test filtrate with pH paper.

activities.title: Plants and soil pH
activities.summary: Grow Hydrangea, Clematis, or other plants; relate growth to soil acidity/alkalinity.

activities.title: Family of salts
activities.summary: Test pH of salts NaCl, Na₂CO₃, NaHCO₃, KNO₃, NH₄Cl with pH paper or universal indicator.

activities.title: Water of crystallisation
activities.summary: Heat hydrated copper sulphate; add water to white anhydrous sample; observe colour return.

exercise_mcqs.question: A solution turns red litmus blue, its pH is likely to be
exercise_mcqs.explanation: Basic solutions turn red litmus blue; pH > 7 — here pH 10.

exercise_mcqs.question: A solution reacts with crushed egg-shells to give a gas that turns lime-water milky. The solution contains
exercise_mcqs.explanation: Egg shells contain CaCO₃; acids release CO₂ that turns lime water milky — HCl is an acid.

exercise_mcqs.question: 10 mL of a solution of NaOH is found to be completely neutralised by 8 mL of a given solution of HCl. If we take 20 mL of the same solution of NaOH, the amount HCl solution (the same solution as before) required to neutralise it will be
exercise_mcqs.explanation: Double the NaOH volume requires double the HCl: 2 × 8 mL = 16 mL.

exercise_mcqs.question: Which one of the following types of medicines is used for treating indigestion?
exercise_mcqs.explanation: Antacids neutralise excess stomach acid to relieve indigestion.

intext_samples.question: Why should curd and sour substances not be kept in brass and copper vessels?
options: Acids react with metal to form toxic compounds
intext_samples.explanation: Acids in curd react with copper/brass (Cu/Zn) forming salts that can be harmful.

intext_samples.question: Which gas is usually liberated when an acid reacts with a metal?
intext_samples.explanation: Acid + metal → salt + hydrogen gas (e.g. Zn + HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂).

intext_samples.question: Why does an aqueous solution of an acid conduct electricity?
options: Due to H⁺ (hydronium) ions in solution
intext_samples.explanation: Acids produce H⁺(aq) ions in water which carry current.

intext_samples.question: While diluting an acid, why is it recommended that the acid should be added to water and not water to the acid?
options: Adding water to acid can cause splashing due to large heat release
intext_samples.explanation: Dilution is highly exothermic; adding water to concentrated acid can splash hot acid — add acid to water slowly.

intext_samples.question: A neutral solution has a pH of
intext_samples.explanation: pH 7 is neutral; below 7 acidic, above 7 basic.

intext_samples.question: An aqueous solution of sodium carbonate turns red litmus blue. It is
intext_samples.explanation: Na₂CO₃ is a salt of strong base and weak acid — its solution is basic.
